title: Replace sscanf log parsing with PCRE2
summary: Pull groups out of the ovector with pcre2_match_data_create_from_pattern, and tell no match apart from an error.

turns.user: want parse_log_line on pcre2. more patterns are coming and sscanf is painful. 0 for no match, -1 if something broke

assistant.body: Sure! Compile the pattern with PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED, then pcre2_match_data_create_from_pattern sizes the match data for exactly the groups it has. On a match the ovector holds a start and end offset per group, so group i runs from ov[2 * i] up to ov[2 * i + 1]. Note: pcre2_match returns PCRE2_ERROR_NOMATCH when nothing matches, and any other negative value is a real error, so those two need separate handling. The match data and the code are freed on every path.

turns.user: build fails in pcre2.h, something like PCRE2_CODE_UNIT_WIDTH must be defined

assistant.body: Apologies, I missed that. pcre2.h has to know whether you want the 8, 16 or 32 bit library before it is included, and it uses PCRE2_CODE_UNIT_WIDTH to map names like pcre2_compile to pcre2_compile_8. These are char strings, so define it as 8 just above the include. The library to link is -lpcre2-8.

turns.user: also prod logs have lowercase error: too. catch both

assistant.body: Here's the idea: leave the pattern alone and let a compile option absorb it. With PCRE2_CASELESS, [A-Z]+ matches lowercase as well. The level keeps whatever case the log used, so compare it with strcasecmp.
